map.It must be spent by the end of every mon: Unused money is forfeited when the plan year ends
map.It can only be used by employers to pay: It is an employer account that pays company business expenses
map.It pays for any expense with no rules or: It lets you spend on non-medical items without a tax penalty

ww.Unused money is forfeited when the plan: HSA funds belong to the owner and roll over from year to year, so there is no use-it-or-lose-it rule; that rule belongs to a flexible spending account.
ww.It is an employer account that pays comp: An HSA is owned by the individual and pays that person's qualified medical costs. Employers may contribute, but the account does not cover company bills.
ww.It lets you spend on non-medical items w: Withdrawals for non-medical items are taxed and usually penalized. Tax-free treatment applies only when the money goes to qualified medical expenses.

map.Only the government and its agencies tha: Drug makers and medical device manufacturers
map.Only insurance salespeople, who sell pol: Auto and life insurance companies and their agents
map.Only patients who are treated in hospita: Patients who ask for copies of their own records

ww.Drug makers and medical device manufactu: Manufacturers are not covered entities under HIPAA. The rules bind providers, health plans, clearinghouses and their business associates that handle protected health information.
ww.Auto and life insurance companies and th: Auto and life insurers are not health plans, so HIPAA does not apply to them. The rules cover healthcare providers, health plans and their business associates.
ww.Patients who ask for copies of their own: Patients are the people HIPAA protects, and they hold rights to their records. The duty to follow the rules falls on organizations that handle health information.

map.A patient being told about the risks onl: A relative agreeing to treatment for a capable adult patient
map.A doctor deciding on a treatment without: A doctor's recommendation of the best treatment for the patient

ww.A relative agreeing to treatment for a c: A capable adult must give consent personally after understanding the risks and benefits. A relative's agreement cannot replace the patient's own informed decision.
ww.A doctor's recommendation of the best tr: A recommendation is just advice. Informed consent needs the patient to understand the risks and benefits and then agree, so the doctor's opinion alone does not count.

map.An order to refuse all treatment of any: An order to stop medicines and comfort care for a patient
map.An order to try CPR in every case, whate: An order to place a patient in intensive care after surgery

ww.An order to stop medicines and comfort c: A DNR covers CPR only. The patient still receives medicines, comfort care and other treatment, so it does not end ordinary care.
ww.An order to place a patient in intensive: A DNR is about whether to attempt CPR if the heart or breathing stops. It has nothing to do with where a patient is placed after surgery.

map.A law that creates new hospitals in ever: A law that makes Medicare available to people of all ages
map.A law that sets doctor salaries at a fix: A law that protects the privacy of patient health records

ww.A law that makes Medicare available to p: The ACA expanded coverage through marketplaces, subsidies and Medicaid expansion. It did not open Medicare to everyone, and Medicare still depends on age or disability.
ww.A law that protects the privacy of patie: Privacy of health records is the purpose of HIPAA. The ACA deals with insurance access and coverage standards, not record privacy.

map.A law that limits visitor hours in a hos: A law that protects the privacy of patient records held by hospitals and clinics
map.A law that bans emergency rooms in every: A law that gives workers unpaid leave to care for a newborn or a sick family member

ww.A law that protects the privacy of patie: Record privacy is covered by HIPAA. EMTALA deals with emergency care, requiring hospitals to screen and stabilize patients regardless of their ability to pay.
ww.A law that gives workers unpaid leave to: Job-protected family leave comes from the FMLA. EMTALA instead requires emergency departments to screen and stabilize patients who arrive, whatever they can pay.

ww.Statistics: STAT comes from the Latin statim, meaning immediately. It tells staff the order is urgent and must be done right away, and it has nothing to do with data or statistics.
ww.Daily: Daily would describe a routine schedule, but STAT means immediately. The term flags an urgent order that cannot wait for a regular cycle.

map.Tear out the page and replace it with a: Cross it out with a marker so it cannot be read
map.Erase it completely and write the new en: Write the correction over the mistake in the same space

ww.Cross it out with a marker so it cannot: Blacking out an entry hides the original and looks like tampering. A proper correction keeps the error legible with a single line, then adds a date and initials.
ww.Write the correction over the mistake in: Writing over a mistake hides the original text and makes the change untraceable. The error should stay readable under a single line, with the correction dated and initialed.

map.Booking only half of the available slots: Leaving open slots for urgent add-on visits
map.Booking appointments after hours only ea: Booking patients in the evening to extend clinic hours

ww.Leaving open slots for urgent add-on vis: Holding slots for urgent visits is a planning practice, not double-booking. Double-booking means two patients are given the same time slot.
ww.Booking patients in the evening to exten: Evening appointments simply extend availability. Double-booking is when two patients are assigned to the same time slot, whatever the hour.

map.Filing every insurance claim for the pat: Submitting insurance claims and collecting patient payments
map.Cleaning patient rooms and halls on all: Managing the daily work schedules of nursing staff

ww.Submitting insurance claims and collecti: Claims and collections are handled by the billing staff. The governing board works at a higher level, setting policy and overseeing quality, finances and leadership.
ww.Managing the daily work schedules of nur: Daily staff scheduling is a job for unit managers. The governing board sets policy and oversees quality, finances and leadership for the whole hospital.

map.They prevent all errors in every kind of: They replace clinical judgment with automatic decisions
map.They make all care free for all of the p: They remove the need for patients to sign consent forms

ww.They replace clinical judgment with auto: Electronic records support clinicians but do not replace their judgment. Their benefit is fast, accurate sharing of information between providers.
ww.They remove the need for patients to sig: Consent is still required whether records are paper or electronic. Electronic records mainly help providers share accurate information quickly.

map.Speaking only one language at work and u: Learning the medical terms used in each specialty
map.Treating every patient identically, what: Following one standard script to keep care fair

ww.Learning the medical terms used in each: Medical vocabulary is useful, but it is not cultural competence. Cultural competence means understanding and respecting patients' diverse backgrounds and beliefs.
ww.Following one standard script to keep ca: A single script ignores differences in language, beliefs and needs. Cultural competence adapts communication and care to fit each patient's background.

map.Care focused only on billing and on the: Care organized around insurance coverage and claim approval rules
map.Care without patient input into the plan: Care planned by the physician and explained after the fact

ww.Care organized around insurance coverage: Organizing care around coverage rules puts payers ahead of the patient. Patient-centered care responds to the patient's needs, values and preferences.
ww.Care planned by the physician and explai: Explaining a plan after it is set leaves the patient out of the decision. Patient-centered care involves patients in choices as they are made.

map.It lowers the quality of care for every: It reduces the number of staff a hospital needs to hire
map.It is only for decoration in the files o: It is kept mainly for hospital marketing and staff schedules

ww.It reduces the number of staff a hospita: Documentation does not replace staff. It supports patient care, legal protection and billing by recording what was done and why.
ww.It is kept mainly for hospital marketing: Records are clinical and legal documents, not marketing or scheduling tools. They guide care, show what was done and support billing.

map.Care only in the last days of life for t: Care that starts after doctors stop treatments meant to cure the illness
map.Cosmetic procedures done to change looks: Therapy that helps patients regain movement and strength after an injury

ww.Care that starts after doctors stop trea: Palliative care does not wait until curative treatment ends. It can begin at any stage of a serious illness and run alongside treatment meant to cure.
ww.Therapy that helps patients regain movem: Regaining movement after injury describes rehabilitation. Palliative care focuses on relieving symptoms and stress of a serious illness.

map.Only holiday parties and social events h: Job promotion rules and long-term career advancement plans
map.Only parking rules and the places where: Marketing strategy and plans for new hospital services
map.Only uniforms and the dress codes that s: Advanced clinical procedures for specialist physicians

ww.Job promotion rules and long-term career: Career paths may be discussed later, but orientation must cover essentials such as safety, infection control, confidentiality and emergency procedures.
ww.Marketing strategy and plans for new hos: Marketing plans are management topics. Orientation covers what new staff need right away: safety, infection control, confidentiality and emergency procedures.
ww.Advanced clinical procedures for special: Advanced procedures are taught through specialty training, not general orientation. Orientation covers safety, infection control, confidentiality and emergency procedures for new staff.

map.Hiring only disabled workers and refusin: Hiring a set quota of disabled workers each year
map.Ignoring disability and treating all wor: Minimum wage and overtime pay for hourly workers

ww.Hiring a set quota of disabled workers e: The ADA sets no hiring quota. It bars discrimination and requires reasonable accommodations for qualified employees with disabilities.
ww.Minimum wage and overtime pay for hourly: Minimum wage and overtime come from wage laws, not the ADA. The ADA requires reasonable accommodations for qualified employees with disabilities.

map.Free insurance for all employees who wor: Paid sick days for employees who have a cold or the flu
map.Paid vacation of several weeks each year: Wage replacement of half pay while an employee is on leave

ww.Paid sick days for employees who have a: FMLA covers longer serious health conditions and family needs through unpaid leave. It does not create paid sick days for short illnesses.
ww.Wage replacement of half pay while an em: FMLA leave is unpaid. It protects the job and health coverage during up to 12 weeks, but it does not replace wages.

map.Using one password for all of the system: Requiring staff to choose a longer password and change it on a set schedule
map.Sharing logins between staff so that any: Scrambling stored patient data so it cannot be read if the device is stolen

ww.Requiring staff to choose a longer passw: A longer, changed password is still one factor. Multi-factor authentication requires a second, different kind of proof, such as a code sent to a phone.
ww.Scrambling stored patient data so it can: Scrambling stored data is encryption, which protects data at rest. Multi-factor authentication checks identity at login with more than one form of proof.

map.Public access to all of the records in t: Letting patients log in to view their own records online
map.Access based on seniority only, so the l: Access that expires automatically after a set number of minutes
map.Giving everyone full access to all of th: Requiring a second code in addition to the password

ww.Letting patients log in to view their ow: A patient portal gives patients access to their own data. Role-based access limits staff to the information their job duties require.
ww.Access that expires automatically after: Automatic expiry is a session timeout. Role-based access instead ties what a user can see to their job role and need to know.
ww.Requiring a second code in addition to t: A second code is multi-factor authentication, which checks identity at login. Role-based access controls what a user can see once logged in.

ww.Inpatient hospital care: Inpatient hospital care is covered by Part A. Part D is the prescription drug benefit, offered through private plans.
ww.Dental exams: Original Medicare generally does not cover routine dental exams. Part D is the prescription drug benefit, offered through private plans.
ww.Outpatient doctor visits: Outpatient doctor visits fall under Part B. Part D is the prescription drug benefit, offered through private plans.

map.A less effective drug that is made by a: A cheaper drug with a weaker dose and fewer safety checks
map.A herbal remedy made from plants that is: A medication that is sold over the counter without a doctor's prescription

ww.A cheaper drug with a weaker dose and fe: Generics must match the brand drug's active ingredient, strength and safety standards, and the FDA reviews them. Lower price does not mean lower quality.
ww.A medication that is sold over the count: Over-the-counter status describes how a drug is sold, not what a generic is. A generic shares the active ingredient of a brand-name drug and usually costs less.

map.Using medical jargon with the patient in: Giving a detailed pamphlet with technical terms
map.Handing over a long form only, to be rea: Speaking louder so the patient hears each word

ww.Giving a detailed pamphlet with technica: Technical pamphlets are hard for patients with low health literacy to follow. Plain language and teach-back confirm real understanding.
ww.Speaking louder so the patient hears eac: Volume does not improve understanding of complex terms. Plain language and teach-back address low health literacy directly.

map.Only for children who are treated at a c: When a patient asks for a longer visit
map.Only for staff who work in the hospital: When a patient is anxious about a procedure
map.Never, as patients should use their own: When a family member can translate a few words

ww.When a patient asks for a longer visit: A longer visit does not solve a language barrier. A qualified interpreter is used when a patient has limited English proficiency.
ww.When a patient is anxious about a proced: Anxiety calls for reassurance and clear explanation, not an interpreter. Interpreters are used when a language barrier affects communication.
ww.When a family member can translate a few: Relatives may mistranslate or omit details and can compromise privacy. Qualified interpreters give accurate, complete communication.

map.Managing by rules only, and giving staff: Rewarding staff with pay for meeting set targets and punishing misses
map.Micromanaging every task and checking th: Letting the group vote on each decision with equal say

ww.Rewarding staff with pay for meeting set: Reward and punishment for targets is transactional leadership. Transformational leaders inspire staff with a vision and encourage them to exceed expectations.
ww.Letting the group vote on each decision: Group voting describes a democratic style. Transformational leaders inspire followers with a vision and drive change.

map.Constant supervision of the staff by a l: A leader who rewards good results and corrects mistakes with penalties
map.Strict control by a leader who sets ever: A leader who inspires staff with a shared vision of change

ww.A leader who rewards good results and co: Rewards and penalties describe transactional leadership. A laissez-faire leader steps back and gives team members freedom with little direction.
ww.A leader who inspires staff with a share: Inspiring through a shared vision is transformational leadership. Laissez-faire means leaving decisions to the team with little direction.

map.Families decide always, whatever the wis: The duty of staff to do no harm to the patient
map.The hospital decides every part of the c: The duty to treat patients fairly and share resources equitably

ww.The duty of staff to do no harm to the p: Doing no harm is the principle of nonmaleficence. Autonomy is the patient's right to make informed decisions about care.
ww.The duty to treat patients fairly and sh: Fair treatment is the principle of justice. Autonomy is the patient's right to make informed decisions about their own care.

map.Only staffing levels on the wards counte: The number of nurses assigned to each ward
map.Only billing and the size of the bills s: The amount the hospital charges for each treatment
map.Only clinical outcomes such as survival: How long patients stay in the hospital before discharge

ww.The number of nurses assigned to each wa: Staffing levels are an operational measure of resources. Patient experience captures how patients perceive communication, responsiveness and respect.
ww.The amount the hospital charges for each: Charges are a financial figure and do not show how patients felt about their care. Patient experience measures their perceptions.
ww.How long patients stay in the hospital b: Length of stay is an operational measure. Patient experience is about patients' perceptions, such as communication and responsiveness.

ww.Twice a day: Twice a day is written BID, from bis in die. TID comes from ter in die and means three times a day.
ww.Once a day: Once a day is written QD or daily. TID comes from ter in die and means three times a day.

map.It increases costs only, with no gain in: It lowers the hospital's cost of supplies
map.It has no effect on the money that a hos: It decides how many beds the hospital can staff

ww.It lowers the hospital's cost of supplie: Payer mix concerns who pays and how much, not supply prices. A favorable mix has more commercial payers, who usually reimburse more than government programs.
ww.It decides how many beds the hospital ca: Bed staffing depends on budget, demand and workforce. Payer mix affects revenue because payers reimburse at different rates.

map.Only active members of the military and: Active-duty military members and their immediate family
map.Only employees of hospitals who have wor: Anyone who has worked at a hospital for ten years
map.Only people with low income, whatever th: Adults and children with low income and limited assets

ww.Active-duty military members and their i: Military families are covered through TRICARE, not Medicare. Medicare eligibility rests on age 65 or older or on certain disabilities.
ww.Anyone who has worked at a hospital for: Where someone works does not decide Medicare eligibility. Age 65 or older, or certain disabilities, qualifies a person.
ww.Adults and children with low income and: Low income and limited assets are the test for Medicaid. Medicare is based on age or disability, whatever a person earns.

map.A department that only costs money, such: A department that supports operations, such as housekeeping
map.A department that sets the price of ever: A department that audits the hospital's finances, such as accounting

ww.A department that supports operations, s: Housekeeping supports operations but does not bill for services, so it is a cost center. A revenue center, such as radiology, brings in income.
ww.A department that audits the hospital's: Accounting is a support function that tracks money rather than earning it. A revenue center generates income by billing for patient services.

map.Access given only to the person who owns: Encryption of records while they are sent between hospitals
map.Access based on seniority only, so the l: Access that records which user opened each patient chart

ww.Encryption of records while they are sen: Encryption protects data in transit. Role-based access limits what each user can see according to their job duties.
ww.Access that records which user opened ea: Recording who opened a chart is an audit trail. Role-based access limits what each user can see according to their job duties.

map.A permanent guarantee that the worker wi: A fixed-term contract that ends on a set date unless it is renewed
map.A time when employees must work without: A time when new employees are paid less than the legal minimum wage

ww.A fixed-term contract that ends on a set: A fixed-term contract has an end date. A probationary period is an early review of performance in a job that may continue afterward.
ww.A time when new employees are paid less: Probationary employees are paid at least the legal minimum wage. Probation means performance is reviewed closely, not that pay is cut below the law.

map.Avoid asking patients questions at all: Diagnose conditions without a physical exam
map.Shorten visits at all costs for the day: Speed up billing and insurance claims

ww.Diagnose conditions without a physical e: Diagnosis needs examination and testing. Active listening helps staff understand patient needs and prevent errors by paying careful attention.
ww.Speed up billing and insurance claims: Billing speed depends on coding and payer processes. Active listening improves understanding of patient needs and prevents errors.

map.Messages sent in spoken words only, with: Messages delivered by phone call or voice mail
map.Messages that nobody can understand or m: Messages sent through a translator or interpreter

ww.Messages delivered by phone call or voic: Phone calls and voice mails use spoken words, which is verbal communication. Nonverbal communication uses body language, tone and facial expression.
ww.Messages sent through a translator or in: Interpreting converts spoken words from one language to another, which is verbal. Nonverbal messages come from body language, tone and expression.

map.Services that a patient wants but which: Services that are experimental and have not been tested in trials
map.Services offered for convenience only, w: Services that cost the most and are billed at full price

ww.Services that are experimental and have: Experimental services lack proven benefit and are often not covered. Medical necessity means a service is reasonable and needed to diagnose or treat a condition.
ww.Services that cost the most and are bill: Price does not decide medical necessity. A necessary service is reasonable and needed to diagnose or treat a condition.

map.Paying for the most services performed b: Paying hospitals for each test and procedure they perform
map.Buying supplies at the lowest price only: Setting payments by the size of the hospital and its bed count

ww.Paying hospitals for each test and proce: Paying per test and procedure is fee for service, which rewards volume. Value-based purchasing adjusts Medicare payments by quality and patient experience scores.
ww.Setting payments by the size of the hosp: Hospital size does not set value-based payments. They are adjusted according to quality and patient experience scores.

map.They are the same thing and mean the tot: Gross is cash received from payers; net is the amount billed to patients
map.Net is before any billing has been done: Net covers inpatient charges, while gross covers charges for outpatient visits

ww.Gross is cash received from payers; net: Gross is the total billed at full charges, not cash received. Net is what the hospital expects to collect after contractual adjustments.
ww.Net covers inpatient charges, while gros: Gross and net are not split by inpatient and outpatient care. Both cover all services, with net coming after contractual adjustments.

map.Those patients use no services at all, s: Those patients require expensive equipment that other patients do not use
map.Those payers never send bills to the hos: Those payers require the hospital to pay a penalty on each admission

ww.Those patients require expensive equipme: These patients use the same services as others. The pressure comes from payment that falls short of cost, not from special equipment.
ww.Those payers require the hospital to pay: Medicaid does not charge admission penalties. The pressure comes from payment that is typically below the cost of care or nothing at all.

map.A budget that never changes once it is a: A budget that is fixed at the start of the year
map.A budget with no numbers in it at all, o: A budget that covers revenue but leaves out expenses

ww.A budget that is fixed at the start of t: A budget fixed in advance is a static budget. A flexible budget adjusts to actual activity levels such as patient volume.
ww.A budget that covers revenue but leaves: A flexible budget covers both revenue and expenses and adjusts as activity changes. Leaving out expenses would not make it flexible.

map.A budget with no spending in it, so that: A budget that cuts each department by the same percent each period
map.A budget with no revenue in it, so that: A budget that is balanced so revenue equals expenses at year end

ww.A budget that cuts each department by th: Across-the-board cuts are not zero-based. A zero-based budget requires each expense to be justified from scratch for the period.
ww.A budget that is balanced so revenue equ: A balanced budget is about the outcome. Zero-based budgeting is a method where each expense is justified from a zero starting point.

map.A forecast for one day only, made at the: A forecast that covers a fixed calendar year and then stops
map.A forecast made once and never changed i: A forecast that looks backward to explain past results

ww.A forecast that covers a fixed calendar: A forecast tied to one calendar year ends when the year does. A rolling forecast is updated regularly and always looks a set period ahead.
ww.A forecast that looks backward to explai: Explaining past results is variance analysis. A rolling forecast looks forward and is updated regularly as new data come in.

map.A physician who treats only skin conditi: A physician who performs operations on the heart and blood vessels
map.A physician who studies the history of m: A physician who specializes in the care of children and teenagers

ww.A physician who performs operations on t: Operating on the heart is the work of a cardiac surgeon. An intensivist cares for critically ill patients in intensive care.
ww.A physician who specializes in the care: Caring for children is pediatrics. An intensivist focuses on critically ill patients of any age in intensive care.

map.Only the doctor's skill, with no other f: The quality of medical care given by local hospitals and clinics
map.Only the prices of medicines, which deci: Medical tests and screenings that doctors offer to detect disease early
map.Only a person's genes, which are passed: Inherited traits and family history of disease passed to children

ww.The quality of medical care given by loc: Medical care is one influence on health, but social determinants are non-medical factors like housing, income and education.
ww.Medical tests and screenings that doctor: Screenings are medical services. Social determinants are conditions of daily life such as housing, income and education.
ww.Inherited traits and family history of d: Inherited traits are biological factors. Social determinants are non-medical conditions such as housing, income and education.

map.A hospital for tests only, with no beds: A hospital that treats patients with serious mental health conditions
map.A hospital for surgeries only, where pat: A hospital that provides short-stay surgery on a planned schedule
map.A hospital for newborns only, where babi: A hospital that specializes in the care of sick infants and children

ww.A hospital that treats patients with ser: That describes a psychiatric hospital. A rehabilitation hospital helps patients recover function after illness or injury through therapy.
ww.A hospital that provides short-stay surg: Short-stay planned surgery describes a surgical center. A rehabilitation hospital offers therapy so patients regain function over time.
ww.A hospital that specializes in the care: That describes a children's hospital. A rehabilitation hospital serves patients of many ages who need to regain lost abilities.

map.Making beds only, with fresh sheets for: Ordering new beds and mattresses from suppliers
map.Cleaning mattresses only, along with oth: Scheduling nurse shifts for each hospital ward

ww.Ordering new beds and mattresses from su: Ordering equipment is purchasing. Bed management coordinates patient placement and bed availability across the hospital.
ww.Scheduling nurse shifts for each hospita: Shift scheduling is a nursing management task. Bed management coordinates patient placement and bed availability across the hospital.

map.An event that never starts because the s: A rare disease that has no known cure and few patients
map.A holiday on which the hospital is close: A known side effect that appears even when proper care is given

ww.A rare disease that has no known cure an: A rare disease is a medical condition, not a care error. A never event is a serious, largely preventable error such as wrong-site surgery.
ww.A known side effect that appears even wh: A known side effect can occur despite proper care, so it is not a preventable error. A never event is a serious error that should not happen.

map.The minimum wage that a hospital must pa: Keeping patient records for the minimum number of years the law requires
map.Sharing all PHI with anyone who asks, fo: Removing names from PHI before it is shared with researchers
map.The minimum number of nurses on each war: Giving patients a copy of their records within a set time

ww.Keeping patient records for the minimum: Record retention is a separate rule. The minimum necessary standard limits how much PHI is used or shared for a given purpose.
ww.Removing names from PHI before it is sha: Removing identifiers is de-identification, a different HIPAA provision. The minimum necessary standard limits PHI use and disclosure to what a purpose needs.
ww.Giving patients a copy of their records: Patient access to records is a separate HIPAA right. The minimum necessary standard limits how much PHI is used or shared.

map.Neither matters in care, since doctors d: Capacity applies to minors, while competence applies to adult patients
map.They are exactly the same thing, so a do: Capacity refers to the clinician's skill, while competence refers to the patient's wishes

ww.Capacity applies to minors, while compet: Both terms apply to adults. Capacity is the clinical ability to make a specific decision, while competence is a legal determination by a court.
ww.Capacity refers to the clinician's skill: Both terms describe the patient's ability to decide, not staff skill or wishes. Capacity is clinical and decision-specific, while competence is a legal determination.

ww.Once a day: Once a day is written QD or daily. QID means four times a day, so a once daily dose would be far too small.
ww.Twice a day: Twice a day is written BID. QID means four times a day, so this gives half the doses the abbreviation calls for.

map.A visit by mail or by post only: A visit booked weeks in advance

ww.A visit by phone call: A phone call is a telephone visit. A walk-in appointment is an in-person visit with no scheduled time.
ww.A visit booked weeks in advance: A visit booked in advance is a scheduled appointment, the opposite of a walk-in, where the patient arrives without a set time.

map.Scheduling by phone only, with no visits: Booking one patient at a time at fixed intervals throughout the day
map.Scheduling at the beach, so that visits: Booking patients by urgency so that the sickest are seen before the rest

ww.Booking one patient at a time at fixed i: One patient per fixed interval is standard scheduling. Wave scheduling books several patients at the start of each hour and sees them in order of arrival.
ww.Booking patients by urgency so that the: Seeing the sickest first is triage. Wave scheduling books several patients at the start of each hour and sees them in order of arrival.

map.Booking months ahead only, with no slots: Booking visits several weeks ahead to keep the calendar full
map.Booking only new patients and turning aw: Limiting visits to patients with a referral from another doctor

ww.Booking visits several weeks ahead to ke: Booking far ahead is traditional scheduling. Open access holds slots so patients can be seen the day they call.
ww.Limiting visits to patients with a refer: Open access does not require a referral. It keeps slots free so patients who call can be seen the same day.

map.A group that only gives goods away to th: A group that raises donations to fund a charitable or public cause
map.A place where people only live and do no: A club whose members meet to share a hobby for fun

ww.A group that raises donations to fund a: A group that raises donations for a cause is a nonprofit or charity. A business provides goods or services to earn a profit.
ww.A club whose members meet to share a hob: A hobby club does not sell goods or services to earn a profit. A business provides goods or services to customers for money.

map.An economy driven by prices and competit: An economy that depends mainly on exports and trade with other countries
map.An economy with no goods to buy or sell: An economy that mixes private business with some government control

ww.An economy that depends mainly on export: Heavy trade describes how an economy sells abroad, not how choices are made. A traditional economy follows customs passed down through generations.
ww.An economy that mixes private business w: Mixing private business and government control is a mixed economy. A traditional economy follows customs and habits passed down through generations.

map.Property that nobody can use, own or sel: Property that a person may use but cannot sell or give away
map.Property owned only by the government an: Property that is rented from a landlord for a limited time

ww.Property that a person may use but canno: Private property can be sold, rented or passed on by its owner. The right to transfer it is part of what makes it private.
ww.Property that is rented from a landlord: Rented property belongs to the landlord, not the renter. Private property is owned by an individual or business, which controls its use.

map.A system where the state runs every busi: A policy of letting goods cross borders without tariffs or quotas
map.Businesses that give everything away fre: A system where workers jointly own and manage the business
map.A system with no laws, rules or limits o: A system where the government sets production goals for firms

ww.A policy of letting goods cross borders: Letting goods cross borders freely is free trade. Free enterprise is the freedom to start and run a business with limited government control.
ww.A system where workers jointly own and m: Joint worker ownership describes a cooperative. Free enterprise is the freedom to start and run a business with limited government control.
ww.A system where the government sets produ: Government production goals are a feature of a command economy. Free enterprise leaves business choices to owners with limited government control.

map.Setting the price of every product and d: Deciding what each factory will produce
map.Making every business decision for all o: Assigning workers to jobs based on a central plan
map.Banning all private businesses in every: Taking over firms that earn large profits

ww.Deciding what each factory will produce: Deciding factory output is central planning in a command economy. A mixed economy leaves most production choices to private firms.
ww.Assigning workers to jobs based on a cen: Assigning jobs by central plan is a command economy feature. A mixed economy leaves most job choices to workers and firms.
ww.Taking over firms that earn large profit: Seizing profitable firms is not a typical role in a mixed economy, where private firms keep their profits and the state sets standards.

map.A cost that changes with every unit made: A cost that rises and falls with the level of output
map.A cost that cannot be paid by a firm in: A cost the firm cannot predict until the end of the year

ww.A cost that rises and falls with the lev: A cost that moves with output is a variable cost, such as materials. A fixed cost, such as rent, stays the same as production changes.
ww.A cost the firm cannot predict until the: Fixed costs are known in advance, such as rent or insurance. They do not change with the amount produced.

map.A tax on large companies that is paid ev: A permit from the city that allows a firm to open
map.A business that never charges fees, as i: A business owned and run by several partners who share profits

ww.A permit from the city that allows a fir: A permit is a license from the government. A franchise is a business that uses another company's brand and system for a fee.
ww.A business owned and run by several part: Several partners sharing profits describes a partnership. A franchise uses another company's brand and system for a fee.

map.Only the owner's hobbies and leisure tim: Employee payroll records and tax forms
map.Only the date of opening and the address: Receipts and invoices from past customers

ww.Employee payroll records and tax forms: Payroll and tax forms belong to operating records, not a plan. A business plan includes goals, market, finances and marketing plans.
ww.Receipts and invoices from past customer: A new business has no past invoices. A business plan includes goals, market, finances and marketing plans.
ww.Customer complaints and product returns: Complaints and returns come from operating experience. A business plan sets out goals, market, finances and marketing plans.

map.Buying goods by mail only, with no use o: Buying and selling goods through a catalog and phone orders
map.Selling only in physical stores, where b: Selling goods at outdoor markets and trade fairs

ww.Buying and selling goods through a catal: Catalog and phone orders are traditional mail order. E-commerce is buying and selling over the internet.
ww.Selling goods at outdoor markets and tra: Markets and trade fairs are in-person selling. E-commerce is buying and selling over the internet.

map.Learning only from books and from printe: Earning a degree and then stopping formal study
map.Learning only in high school, with that: Taking one training course when starting a new job

ww.Earning a degree and then stopping forma: Stopping after a degree is the opposite of lifelong learning, which means continuing to learn new skills throughout your career.
ww.Taking one training course when starting: One course at the start of a job does not meet the idea. Lifelong learning continues to build new skills throughout your career.

map.Only how close it is to a friend: The brand name of the employer
map.Only the color of the office walls: The number of employees in the building

ww.The brand name of the employer: A well-known name does not tell you about pay, duties or hours. Reviewing pay, benefits, duties and schedule shows whether the job fits.
ww.The number of employees in the building: Building size does not show whether the job suits you. Pay, benefits, duties and schedule are what to review before accepting.

map.Only credit cards and debit cards used i: Valuable items such as jewels and art kept as a store of wealth
map.Only things you can touch, such as coins: The wealth a person holds in houses and land
map.Only gold bars held in a vault by a bank: The income a worker earns from a job each year

ww.Valuable items such as jewels and art ke: Jewels and art hold value but are not widely accepted as payment. Money is anything widely accepted for goods and services.
ww.The wealth a person holds in houses and: Houses and land are assets but not widely accepted as payment. Money is anything widely accepted for goods and services.
ww.The income a worker earns from a job eac: Income is money earned over time, not what money is. Money is anything widely accepted as payment for goods and services.

map.An organization that never earns revenue: An organization run by the government to provide services to the public
map.An organization owned by shareholders wh: A business that donates a share of its sales to charity but pays its owners

ww.An organization run by the government to: Government-run bodies belong to the public sector. A nonprofit is a private organization that uses its income for a mission.
ww.A business that donates a share of its s: A business that pays its owners is for-profit even if it gives to charity. A nonprofit has no owners to pay.

map.The part owned by charities only, funded: The part of the economy that makes goods for export
map.The part run by the government and its a: The part of the economy that operates without paying taxes

ww.The part of the economy that makes goods: Exporting describes where goods are sold. The private sector is defined by ownership by individuals and companies.
ww.The part of the economy that operates wi: Private firms pay taxes like others. The private sector is the part of the economy owned by individuals and companies.

map.Guaranteed profit in every year of tradi: Receiving a steady salary from the first day
map.No need to work hard to run the business: Having a boss who sets the hours and tasks

ww.Receiving a steady salary from the first: A steady salary is typical of employment. Business owners face the risk of losing the money they invested if the business fails.
ww.Having a boss who sets the hours and tas: Owners usually set their own hours and tasks. The real risk of ownership is losing the money invested if the business fails.

map.Only the government and its agencies: A loan used to start a firm
map.Only the competitors of the business: A document stating the firm's goals
map.Only the owner, as no one else is affect: A tax paid on the firm's profits

ww.A loan used to start a firm: A loan is a financial tool, not a person or group. A stakeholder is anyone affected by a business's decisions.
ww.A document stating the firm's goals: A document is not a person or group. A stakeholder is anyone affected by a business's decisions, such as workers or customers.
ww.A tax paid on the firm's profits: A tax is a payment, not a person or group. A stakeholder is anyone affected by a business's decisions, such as workers or customers.

ww.Market economy: A market economy relies on prices and competition, with buyers and sellers making choices. A traditional economy relies on customs.
ww.Command economy: A command economy relies on government plans. A traditional economy relies on customs passed down through generations.

map.Customs control every choice: Production is set by central plans

ww.Production is set by central plans: Central plans describe a command economy. A weakness of a free market is that people with little money may lack basic needs.
ww.Firms cannot keep their profits: Firms keep their profits in a free market. A real weakness is that people with little money may lack basic needs.

map.Public goods always lose money by law, s: Governments want to earn extra profit from goods that firms sell too cheaply
map.Private firms are banned from making goo: Public goods cost too little for private firms to bother producing

ww.Governments want to earn extra profit fr: Governments do not provide public goods to earn profit. They do so because private firms struggle to charge users.
ww.Public goods cost too little for private: Cost is not the main issue. Private firms avoid public goods because users are hard to charge, so they cannot earn a return.

map.Partners never disagree on any matter: Partners pay no tax on their share of profits
map.Profits belong to one person only, the o: Owners are protected from the firm's debts

ww.Partners pay no tax on their share of pr: Partners pay tax on their share of profits. A real advantage is sharing money, skills and work.
ww.Owners are protected from the firm's deb: General partners are usually responsible for the firm's debts. A real advantage is sharing money, skills and work.

map.It pays no taxes on any income that it e: The business has an unlimited life even if a partner leaves
map.Only one person decides for the firm and: One owner keeps all profits and makes the decisions

ww.The business has an unlimited life even: A partnership often ends when a partner leaves or dies, unless it is restructured. A real disadvantage is disagreement and shared liability.
ww.One owner keeps all profits and makes th: One owner making decisions describes a sole proprietorship. In a partnership decisions and profits are shared among partners.

map.It pays no taxes at all on its profits: It is simple and cheap to form with little paperwork
map.It is always owned and run by one person: Owners must repay the firm's debts from personal assets

ww.It is simple and cheap to form with litt: Corporations require filings, bylaws and fees, so forming one is more complex. The key advantage is limited liability for owners.
ww.Owners must repay the firm's debts from: Corporate owners usually cannot lose personal assets to the firm's debts. That risk applies to sole proprietorships and general partnerships.

map.No fees to pay to the brand owner at all: Lower start-up cost than an independent shop
map.A guaranteed profit for the owner each y: Ownership of the brand and its trademarks

ww.Lower start-up cost than an independent: Franchises often cost more to start because of fees. The advantage is a proven system and brand recognition.
ww.Ownership of the brand and its trademark: The franchisor owns the brand and trademarks. The franchisee gets a proven system and brand recognition.

map.Business done only in one town, with no: Business that sells to other businesses
map.Business done only online by one company: Business that trades within a single country's borders
map.Business done without customers or buyer: Business that is run mostly from the owner's home

ww.Business that sells to other businesses: Selling to other businesses is B2B and can be local. Global business operates or trades across countries.
ww.Business that trades within a single cou: Trade within one country is domestic business. Global business operates or trades across countries.
ww.Business that is run mostly from the own: Where the owner works does not make a business global. Global business trades across countries.

map.It guarantees a job in any field that yo: It lets you skip interviews when applying for jobs
map.It lets you avoid all of your weaknesses: It shows you the exact salary you will earn

ww.It lets you skip interviews when applyin: Strengths do not remove interviews. Knowing them helps you choose careers where those strengths matter.
ww.It shows you the exact salary you will e: Strengths do not set pay. Knowing them helps you pick careers where those strengths matter.

map.Homework assignments that students do at: Classes that count toward a high school diploma
map.Required classes that all students must: Grades earned on report cards each term

ww.Classes that count toward a high school: Classes toward a diploma are part of the regular curriculum. Extracurricular activities take place outside regular classes.
ww.Grades earned on report cards each term: Grades are results of coursework. Extracurricular activities are optional clubs and sports outside regular classes.

map.Nothing at all, as you have no skills to: Your social media photos and follower counts
map.Made-up jobs that you never held at any: Jobs held by your parents or relatives

ww.Your social media photos and follower co: Social media content does not show workplace skills. School activities, volunteering and relevant skills do.
ww.Jobs held by your parents or relatives: Relatives' jobs say nothing about your own skills. Use your school activities, volunteering and relevant skills.

map.Only the workers who are paid wages by t: A financial statement that lists the assets and debts of the firm
map.Only the government agencies that collec: A written contract that sets prices between a firm and a supplier
map.Only the competitors who sell similar go: A yearly report that shows the sales and costs of the firm

ww.A financial statement that lists the ass: A financial statement is a document, not a person or group. A stakeholder is anyone affected by the business.
ww.A written contract that sets prices betw: A contract is a document, not a person or group. A stakeholder is anyone affected by the business.
ww.A yearly report that shows the sales and: A report is a document, not a person or group. A stakeholder is anyone affected by the business.

map.A guaranteed profit in the first year: A loyal base of repeat customers
map.Customers who always pay in advance: A strong brand name known by buyers

ww.A loyal base of repeat customers: Loyal customers are a benefit. A new business risks failing to attract enough customers.
ww.A strong brand name known by buyers: A known brand helps sales and is not a risk. New firms risk failing to attract enough customers.

map.A ban on all imports, so that only goods: A tax placed on imported goods to protect home industries
map.Trade that takes place only inside a sin: The movement of people from farms to cities
map.The state taking over every firm so that: The shift of production from factories to online services

ww.A tax placed on imported goods to protec: A tax on imports is a tariff, a protectionist tool. Globalization is the growing connection of economies and cultures through trade.
ww.The movement of people from farms to cit: People moving to cities is urbanization. Globalization is the growing connection of economies and cultures worldwide.
ww.The shift of production from factories t: That shift is a change in industry mix. Globalization is the growing worldwide connection of economies through trade.

map.It pays no taxes on any income that it e: Sales are taxed once at purchase and again when resold
map.Owners pay tax on firm profits only once: Owners are taxed on profits and again on any loans they take

ww.Sales are taxed once at purchase and aga: That describes taxes on sales. Double taxation in a C corporation means profits are taxed at the firm and again as shareholder dividends.
ww.Owners are taxed on profits and again on: Loans are not taxed as income. Double taxation means profits are taxed at the firm and again on dividends.

map.Fixed costs only: Total cost divided by units made

ww.Revenue divided by units sold: Revenue divided by units is the average price. Total cost is fixed costs plus variable costs.
ww.Total cost divided by units made: That gives average cost per unit. Total cost is fixed costs plus variable costs.

map.Output always rises faster as inputs are: Output rises faster as more inputs are used
map.Costs fall forever as output rises: Costs fall as a firm produces more units
map.Output never changes as inputs rise: Prices fall when more of a good is supplied

ww.Output rises faster as more inputs are u: Faster rising output is increasing returns. Diminishing returns means extra inputs add less and less extra output.
ww.Costs fall as a firm produces more units: Falling average costs describe economies of scale. Diminishing returns means extra inputs add less extra output.
ww.Prices fall when more of a good is suppl: Price falling with supply is a market effect. Diminishing returns is about smaller output gains from added inputs.

map.Only the number of units, because the pr: Whether the firm's advertising costs have gone down
map.Nothing, because fewer units always mean: Whether the new price is higher than competitors
map.Nothing, because a higher price always m: How many new stores competitors plan to open

ww.Whether the firm's advertising costs hav: Advertising costs are secondary. The business must check whether total revenue and profit rose or fell.
ww.Whether the new price is higher than com: Comparing with competitors does not show profit. The firm should check whether total revenue and profit rose or fell.
ww.How many new stores competitors plan to: Competitors' plans do not reveal the firm's own results. The firm should check whether revenue and profit rose or fell.

map.A product sold only to employees at a de: A product sold at a high price because it is rare
map.A product that the firm makes at a loss: A product that is recalled because of a safety problem

ww.A product sold at a high price because i: A rare, high priced product is the opposite. A loss leader is sold at a low price to attract customers.
ww.A product that is recalled because of a: A recalled product is withdrawn from sale. A loss leader is advertised at a low price to draw customers.

map.To increase the profit on each unit, sin: To raise the margin earned on each unit
map.To stop customers from buying any items: To discourage competitors from stocking the item

ww.To raise the margin earned on each unit: A lower price shrinks the margin on each unit. The aim is to attract buyers and clear stock.
ww.To discourage competitors from stocking: Price cuts target buyers, not competitors. The aim is to attract buyers and clear stock.

map.The government sets the price of every g: Wealth is shared equally among citizens by the state
map.Everyone is guaranteed the same income w: A central office decides what firms produce
map.A central plan removes all waste because: Basic goods are provided at no charge

ww.Wealth is shared equally among citizens: Equal sharing by the state is a command or socialist feature. Markets reward effort and skill with different incomes.
ww.A central office decides what firms prod: Central decisions are a command economy feature. In a market economy prices and competition guide production.
ww.Basic goods are provided at no charge: Goods at no charge are not typical of a market. Prices and competition encourage efficiency and innovation.

map.Only from the government, since banks an: Profits earned in its first year
map.Only from a lottery prize that the owner: Selling shares on a public stock exchange
map.Only from customers, who must pay for al: Government tax refunds from earlier years

ww.Profits earned in its first year: Profits come after a business operates, so they cannot fund the start. Start-up funds come from savings, loans, investors or crowdfunding.
ww.Selling shares on a public stock exchang: A start-up cannot usually list on a stock exchange. Typical sources are savings, loans, investors or crowdfunding.
ww.Government tax refunds from earlier year: Tax refunds are not a reliable start-up source. Entrepreneurs use savings, loans, investors or crowdfunding.

map.A guaranteed profit every month, whateve: Receiving a steady paycheck from an employer each week
map.Freedom from all legal responsibilities: Having the freedom to set your own working hours

ww.Receiving a steady paycheck from an empl: A steady paycheck is typical of employment. Entrepreneurs risk losing the money they invested if the business fails.
ww.Having the freedom to set your own worki: Setting your own hours is a benefit, not a risk. The real risk is losing the money invested if the business fails.

map.The business pays no tax of any kind on: The business is taxed at a lower corporate rate than individuals
map.The business files a separate return and: The owner is taxed on salary but not on retained profit

ww.The business is taxed at a lower corpora: A sole proprietorship has no separate corporate tax. Income is reported on the owner's personal tax return.
ww.The owner is taxed on salary but not on: The owner is taxed on all business profit, whether withdrawn or kept. It is reported on the personal return.

map.Benefits are paid only to workers who ea: Benefits are taxed at a higher rate than regular wages
map.Benefits are always worthless to workers: Benefits raise the base salary on the pay stub

ww.Benefits are taxed at a higher rate than: Benefits such as insurance are often untaxed or lightly taxed. They add value beyond salary, which can justify lower pay.
ww.Benefits raise the base salary on the pa: Benefits are separate from base salary. They add value such as insurance and retirement matches, which can justify lower pay.

map.Only people with full-time jobs: People who hold jobs in factories and offices
map.Only people with a college degree who ar: People aged 16 or older who live in the country

ww.People who hold jobs in factories and of: The labor force includes all kinds of jobs and people seeking work. It is the employed plus those actively seeking work.
ww.People aged 16 or older who live in the: Age and residence alone do not define the labor force. It counts people who are employed or actively seeking work.

ww.$5: Five dollars is the fixed cost per unit, $5,000 divided by 1,000. Adding the $3 variable cost per unit gives an average total cost of $8.
ww.$3: Three dollars is the variable cost per unit. Adding the fixed cost per unit of $5 gives an average total cost of $8.

map.Recording only when cash changes hands,: Recording revenue when cash is received and expenses when paid
map.Recording only profits: Recording sales at forecast values before any work is done

ww.Recording revenue when cash is received: That is cash-basis accounting. Accrual accounting records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of cash timing.
ww.Recording sales at forecast values befor: Accrual accounting records revenue when it is earned, not before. Forecast sales are estimates and are not recorded as revenue.

map.A written document in every case, signed: A written document filed with the court

ww.A notary public stamp: A notary stamp is not required for most contracts. A valid contract needs offer, acceptance and consideration.
ww.A written document filed with the court: Contracts need not be filed with a court. A valid contract needs offer, acceptance and consideration.
ww.Payment made in cash: Payment in cash is not required, since consideration can be a promise. A valid contract needs offer, acceptance and consideration.

ww.A school drama club: A drama club builds performance skills, not business knowledge. FBLA offers business competitions and career learning for high school students.
ww.A yearbook committee: A yearbook committee focuses on publishing a book. FBLA is the student group built for learning about business careers.
